Chapter 6 is finished: the whole range 875.39 → 1010.95 is covered with no gaps, including the ~12.4 s end-screen tail. The speed numbers can't be checked against the 650 ms budget, though. The box is shared and the load average was 13–15 on 4 cores during the tests.

| 60-frame window | ms/frame (load 13–15) | Rough estimate on an idle machine |
|---|---|---|
| Start 26850 (Proxima crash: heaviest live plate frames, plus page load and a one-time ~8 s still pre-render) | 2748 | ~700 |
| Start 29900 (end screen) | 1447 | ~360 |

My estimate for the chapter average is about 380–450 ms/frame. That is extrapolated from those two windows and sampled frames, not measured. Re-run the speed test on an idle machine to confirm.

**What was there:** a calibration stub `ch6.js` (four 1-second test poses with "pose N" debug text, the rest black) and a working plate renderer `ch6_future.js`, which moves the real Blue Marble continents. I kept the renderer unchanged and removed the stub and all debug text.

**What I added:**
- **s097:** chapter card "WHERE IS THE DRIP GOING NEXT?" over the Atlantic. The drip arcs pulse on "going", the Mid-Atlantic Ridge draws on, a 1620 pill lands on "line", and a school bus drops into a widening magma gap on "bus".
- **s098:** a time-scrub bar with a rolling "+N MILLION YEARS" counter, a fast forward spin that fogs over, four "?" marks on "agree", then four tiles grow out of them on "models".
- **s099–s102:** each tile expands into a live globe of one model (Proxima, Novopangaea, Amasia, Aurica). Each has motion arrows, the tracked US marker, an impact flash with camera shake and a thud on contact, and the MODEL pill. Proxima also gets the "+250" counter; Aurica gets the glow on Australia and AU + RICA flying together into the name. Each globe shrinks back into its grid slot.
- **s103:** tiles pulse on Africa / Antarctica / Asia / Australia. The Explorer, on North America of a tiny planet, runs left, runs right, then stands undecided, and a comment bubble pops on "comments". The continents then slide together into a splash on a flat Equal Earth map, with Antarctica left out as in Holden's joke. The Pangooy card flashes for 0.5 s on "Tuesday".
- **s104:** heat map on the Proxima supercontinent with the "LIVABLE FOR MAMMALS: UNDER 1 IN 6" counter rolling 10 → 6. Then the Explorer wilts under red light and heat shimmer and faints exactly on "Reminder", with a soft thud.
- **s105–s106:** tiles become a filmstrip that tears open onto the opening drip globe, and the arcs re-trace on "been". Then a Bacon portrait with a 2026 → 1620 counter, the matching capes, the n246 page underlined on "accident" and turned gold on "right", and Gondwana snapping apart to leave the waving Explorer, ring and porch light on Antarctica.
- **s107–s109:** a filmstrip of paleo stills, today, and the four models, with "today" highlighted on "frame". The blank frame fills with the live globe and flies down to Afar, where the three-armed Y draws and the southern arm creeps south. The end screen puts Afar in the left third and keeps the right side calm: a frame for the next-video tile titled "MYTH JUICE #2: SPLIT IN TWO" (inside left empty) and a glowing subscribe ring.

All 61 sound cues are registered.

**To cut render cost:** once a model's plates settle, after the heat map is fully on, and for the 19 s end screen, the globe is rendered once and held with a slow 2D push-in. The arcs, markers and rift overlays stay live.

**Self-check:** two full passes of about 104 stills each (every 2 s plus every marker) and three targeted passes, all looked at. I fixed an empty-ocean framing on Novopangaea and on the start of Aurica, Aurica plates that never touched, the bus gap and scrub bar, the Pangooy card font, the end-screen framing, text over the white Antarctica, and corner tiles outside the safe margin. Every transition into a held frame is seamless.

**Known issues and deviations:**
- **Model timing:** the script's cues conflict, so the plates start moving on "slams" and the crash lands on "Africa" (897.25), not starting on "crashes".
- **s098 tiles:** each shows today's globe from its own model's camera rather than all centred on North America, so each tile expands seamlessly into its model.
- **Gondwana:** ch5a has no finished Gondwana still yet, so this is my own simplified 2D version built from the paleo track data.
- **Aurica:** the model can't split Eurasia, so the camera stays on the Pacific side.
- **Sounds:** the end-screen "audio logo sting" isn't in the sound library, so it isn't cued. The "felt piano note" is a `bell_small` at -22 dB as a stand-in.
- **Engine bug:** `lib/equalearth.js` doesn't parse (a stray `np.float64`), so I re-implemented the projection in `ch6_lib.js`.

No new images were downloaded. `credits_ch6.json` records the n246 page and the engine assets used.

I've finished ch5a: it now covers every frame from 604.37 to 694.13 with no gaps, and the debug text is gone. The speed target isn't confirmed. The 60-frame test ran at about 2,370 ms/frame, but other renders had the 4-core machine at a load of 10–14. A ch5b segment timed just before it with the same command ran at 4,767 ms/frame, so ch5a costs about half as much. I couldn't get a clean unloaded number, so I can't say whether it's under 650 ms.

**What was there:** `ch5a.js` was only a test scene: a paleo globe with a debug readout in the top-left. `ch5a_data.js` (plate outlines and polygon membership per million years) was usable as-is. `ch5a_paleo.js` had a working plate-rotation renderer, which I kept and extended.

**What I built, by segment:**
- **s072–s073:** chapter card, then the globe rewinds 0 → 180 Ma with a counter. Each continent fills orange on its name. The pieces float slightly apart and snap together on "Gondwana" with the "GONDWANA" headline. A cut to Antarctica shows a pulsing yellow ring and the "keypiece" pill.
- **s074:** framed sepia Bacon portrait over a blurred Novum Organum page, with the quote pill. Back on the assembled globe, white drip arrows converge on the ring at "the whole time".
- **s075:** the clock runs forward, white cracks appear, and a cyan strip of new ocean opens between Africa and Antarctica.
- **s076:** the South Atlantic opens as a zipper (teeth on the closed part, a slider moving north). The last seam glows yellow, then snaps at T≈113 Ma.
- **s077 (Explorer gag, 5.85 s):** he stands on top of a small south-up planet, about 45% of frame height, rim-lit, beside a small cabin. He waves as the continents drift down and out of frame. A yellow ring appears under him on "Antarctica", and the porch light flickers on at "house".
- **s078:** India streaks north with a glowing trail and a speed-tag pill with motion lines and a red/blue siren flash. Africa and Australia crawl with short trails. India hits Asia with shock rings, a flash and shake.
- **s079:** a paper "textbook" diagram: the counter jumps back to 180 Ma, the pieces float, dashed pencil arrows hint at the fit, then they lock. The tips pulse where they meet Antarctica.
- **s080–s081:** a crossfade back to the real Earth. Dotted yellow paths of the three tips draw toward Antarctica, then turn into glowing stitched seams under "THE BIG DRIPS ARE SCARS".

All sound cues from the script are registered, plus a few low-level pops and whooshes. Times follow the markers, and only the script's on-screen texts are used.

**Self-check:** I did five rounds of stills (r1–r5, 74–77 frames each, plus every scene boundary) and looked at each contact sheet. Fixes along the way:
- white lines inside continents
- a lighter patch in the middle of Antarctica (West Antarctica was being drawn as ordinary land)
- seams too short for the zipper to read
- weak gag composition
- a black flash on one cut
- an uneven light direction
- an annotation sitting in the bottom 12% of the frame

To cut render cost I cached Antarctica with the background land and thinned the continent outlines on the whole-globe overlay.

**Known issues:**
- India touches Asia at about 44 Ma on the counter. The reconstruction only closes the gap around 40 Ma; the usual figure is about 50 Ma.
- When South America is highlighted, its southern part stays sand-coloured with a straight cut edge, because it's a separate polygon in the data.
- The southern tip of India's path has a visible hook. That is the real track turning back north between 140 and 180 Ma, softened by smoothing but not removed.
- The cabin's left corner sits slightly off the curve of the planet.

**Engine bug (worked around, not edited):** `www/lib/equalearth.js` contains `np.float64(...)`, so it throws on import. My module doesn't use it.

Files are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/`:
- `engine/www/ep/ep01/ch5a.js` (rewritten)
- `engine/www/ep/ep01/ch5a_paleo.js` (extended)
- `engine/www/ep/ep01/img/ch5a_bacon_n246.jpg` (copy of the public-domain page already used in ch1)
- `engine/www/ep/ep01/credits_ch5a.json`
- `research/chapters/ch5a/r1/` to `r5/` (stills and contact sheets)
- `research/chapters/ch5a/speed.mp4`
